why: Nothing outside a run could learn that it finished. A worker drove a real
run in the background and then slept blind in a loop — fifteen minutes of
waiting for runs that finished in seconds — and an orchestrator wrote
three hand-rolled watchers that were each wrong in a different way,
because the only observables were guessing an interval or watching a file,
and both were used badly (ticfac tick u9l, epic av8; the backlog's run
feed, ticfac tick n0r, proposed for dashboards and independently
motivated by a worker and an orchestrator both waiting badly).
This contract pins the third option: one append-only JSONL event stream
per run, written locally under the run-state root, that a NON-PARTICIPANT
can subscribe to — open the file once and follow the appends — and learn
WHEN TO LOOK. It is the reconciler's journal made readable while the run
is live: the same stages, the same order, with run/tick/attempt identity
on every line so a line can never be mistaken for a verdict.
It is deliberately NOT a record and NOT durable. The durable truth of a
tick is the evidence on the integration branch — commits plus the report
with its STATUS line — and the feed exists so nobody polls that truth or
sleeps against it. A feed line is a hint about when to look; it is never
evidence about what happened. That division is the whole design.

layout.written_by: the reconciler, one line per journal event, at the moment the event happens
layout.classified_by: contracts/ticfac-run-state.json layout.entries — the `.ticfac/logs/` entry. The feed is exhaust, not a record: it is covered by that contract's gitignore fragment, and it never lands on the integration branch.
layout.host_path_is: <run-id> is the run's own id, the same one that names .ticfac/runs/<run-id>/, so a subscriber that knows a run's id knows where its feed is without asking the run

identity.run_id_is: the run's id, the same one that names the run directory and the run tag
identity.tick_id_is: null for run-level events (the run finished, the run resumed); a tick id for everything a tick passed through
identity.attempt_is: null before the tick's first dispatch is recorded and for run-level events; the 1-based attempt number otherwise
identity.required_and_null: tick_id and attempt are required-and-null rather than omittable, for the same reason every nullable provenance field is: a line that omits tick_id and one that states it as null are different claims, and only the second is a claim at all.
identity.attempt_is_1_based: The schema subset has no minimum, so the readers check it beyond the schema: an integer attempt below 1 is refused by both, as an event that claims an attempt that was never dispatched.

append_only.a_reader_resumes_from: the byte offset it stopped at
why: A subscriber must be able to miss nothing: follow the file from offset
zero, or from the offset a previous session remembered, and the lines
between are the events that happened while nobody watched.
A rewritten line is a feed a dashboard cannot trust, and a feed nobody
trusts is one more hand-rolled watcher waiting to be wrong.

subscribe.how: Open the file and follow the appends — read to the end, then each new line as it lands. The follower's own read cadence is an implementation detail of the follower, not a guess about the work; the subscriber never names an interval and never decides anything on one.
subscribe.a_line_means: worth looking now, never 'the work is finished' — the rule tk herd wait's own documentation states, observed exactly: it reported three agents settled while two had zero commits and no report.
subscribe.completion_is_decided_by: durable evidence alone: the commits on the attempt branch plus the report with its STATUS line (ticfac tick 2xu). The feed is not in that list and must never be added to it.
subscribe.a_lost_or_late_or_untruthful_line: changes no verdict. A record written by the thing that may be gone is not evidence of its liveness (Appendix A2): the signal wakes, the evidence decides, and a lost signal is then harmless.
subscribe.why_not_pushed: The feed is local exhaust at the run's write cadence, like the rest of .ticfac/logs/. A hosted mirror is a subscriber like any other — publish to one by following this file, never by making the run push to it.

boundary.why: One writer per run, because two append-only feeds interleaved is neither append-only nor a feed. Workers and non-participants read; a worker that could write its own 'done' line could write a lie, and the whole point of the evidence boundary is that nobody's say-so is the verdict.

schema.description: One line of the run event feed. Closed: a field this schema does not name is a field no reader parses, and a feed that grows a field nobody versioned is a feed that breaks its subscribers silently. `at` is RFC3339 and `attempt` is 1-based — both are checked beyond the schema, because the subset has neither format nor minimum.

schema_version.description: The line schema's version. A subscriber that meets a schema_version it does not know refuses the line rather than guessing at it.

at.description: RFC3339. When the event happened, stamped by the writer at the moment it did.

run_id.description: The run's id — the identity that names .ticfac/runs/<run-id>/ and ticfac/run-<run-id>.

tick_id.description: Null for run-level events. Required-and-null rather than omitted.

attempt.description: The 1-based attempt number the event belongs to. Null before the tick's first dispatch is recorded and for run-level events.

stage.description: The journal stage — dispatched, settled, collected, run_finished — the ordered vocabulary a tick passes through.

detail.description: Human-readable, and deliberately last: it is the line a person reads, not a field a program parses.

feed_event_run_level.detail: completed: every tick closed behind the gate

invalid.why: no run_id — a line without run identity is a line a multi-run dashboard cannot place, which is the one thing the identity on every line exists to prevent
tick_id omitted rather than null — required-and-null is the rule, because 'no tick' and 'the tick was not recorded' are different claims

document.detail: completed: every tick closed behind the gate

invalid.why: attempt omitted rather than null — same rule, same reason

document.detail: completed: every tick closed behind the gate

invalid.why: an unversioned extra field — the schema is closed, because a feed that grows a field no subscriber versioned is a feed that breaks silently
attempt as a string — the identity fields are machine-read by every subscriber, and a string in one of them is a dashboard that sorts attempts alphabetically
invalid.expect_error_contains: $.attempt: value matches none of the anyOf alternatives

invalid.why: a schema_version the feed has never carried — a subscriber that meets an unknown version refuses the line rather than guessing at it, and the fixture holds the readers to that
invalid.expect_error_contains: $.schema_version: 2 is not one of the permitted values
